findings.body: The doc comment promises output of at most `limit` characters, but when `head` contains no space the `None` arm returns `limit` characters plus the `…` glyph, i.e. `limit + 1` characters. The tests already encode this off-by-one with `<= 21` for `limit = 20`, so the code and tests agree but the documented contract is wrong. A caller that passes the exact platform ceiling (e.g. GitHub's check-run title limit) as `limit` can receive a string one character too long, which GitHub may reject or truncate. Reserve one character of the budget for the ellipsis so the output truly fits within `limit`.
findings.title: Keep the ellipsis inside the character limit

value.summary: The new `summarise` module truncates model-authored text on word boundaries using char-aware slicing, which avoids the multibyte panic the comment warns about. The only issue is that `shorten` can return `limit + 1` characters when no space is found, contradicting its own doc comment and risking a title that exceeds the platform ceiling by one character.
